question_text: 40% of students in a class own an orange highlighter, 20% own a blue highlighter, and 50% do not own either coloured highlighter.

subparts.stem: Draw a Venn diagram to describe the situation.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up equation $(0.4 - x) + x + (0.2 - x) = 1 - 0.5$

subparts.solution:
Let $O$ represent a student who owns an orange highlighter, and $B$ represent a student who owns a blue highlighter.
Let the proportion of students in $O \cap B$ be $x$.
$$\therefore \text{the proportion in } O \cap B' \text{ is } 0.4 - x$$
$$\text{and the proportion in } O' \cap B \text{ is } 0.2 - x.$$
$$\text{The proportion in } O' \cap B' \text{ is } 0.5.$$
$$\therefore (0.4 - x) + x + (0.2 - x) = 1 - 0.5$$
$$\therefore 0.6 - x = 0.5$$
$$\therefore x = 0.1$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The sum of probabilities of all disjoint regions in a Venn diagram equals 1.
step_by_step: Then only orange is $0.4 - x$ and only blue is $0.2 - x$.
Therefore, $(0.4 - x) + x + (0.2 - x) = 0.5 \implies 0.6 - x = 0.5 \implies x = 0.1$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Adding the total probabilities $\text{P}(O) + \text{P}(B)$ without subtracting the intersection.

subparts.stem: Find the probability that a randomly selected student owns a blue highlighter, given they own an orange highlighter.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The conditional probability formula is $\text{P}(B \mid O) = \frac{\text{P}(B \cap O)}{\text{P}(O)}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Putting $\text{P}(B)$ in the denominator instead of $\text{P}(O)$.

subparts.stem: Find the probability that a randomly selected student owns an orange highlighter, given they do not own a blue highlighter.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Conditional probability on a complement: $\text{P}(O \mid B') = \frac{\text{P}(O \cap B')}{\text{P}(B')}$.
